claims.statement: The guide applies to FPT, GHES and GHEC and offers clues for remembering a personal-account username, not a tested account recovery procedure.
On macOS Desktop uses GitHub Desktop Preferences; on Windows it uses File Options. Accounts shows username and Git shows the Git email, explicitly not guaranteed to be the primary account address.

The Git user.name configuration may contain a previously configured username, but its local value is not authenticated account identity or proof of current ownership. The source command example is data and is not executed as an identity test.

A personal repository or own fork remote URL may reveal the username immediately following the host; another person's clone reveals their username, while organization repositories reveal the organization rather than the user. Remote names alone cannot identify the acting credential.
Remote strings may also need reconciliation with previously reviewed rename redirects; locating a name does not prove stable identity, live destination ownership or authorized account access.
The cloud-only further-reading pointer links verification guidance, not automatic recovery. No Desktop state, Git settings, credential, browser session or account is changed.
